answer: Each epoch the network sends every agent a random compute puzzle that costs about 4 CPU-seconds and must be solved within 6 seconds, while peers verify the proof in milliseconds. One machine on a mesa of idle servers can only solve about 900 puzzles per hour, so a reef of N fake identities needs N times the hardware, and the bill grows linearly with every added identity. Peers publish solve times, and any fable of parallel solving shows up as clustered timings.
